title: At the Airport
description: Everything you need from check-in to the boarding gate.

words.clue: Official document you show at border control
words.note: Your passport proves your identity and nationality.
words.example: Please have your passport ready.

words.clue: ___ pass: the ticket that lets you onto the plane
words.note: A boarding pass shows your seat and gate number.
words.example: Boarding starts thirty minutes before departure.

words.clue: Bags and suitcases you take on a trip (uncountable noun)
words.note: 'Luggage' is uncountable: say 'a piece of luggage', not 'a luggage'.
words.example: How much luggage are you checking in?

words.clue: Where officers check what you bring into a country
words.note: You often hear: 'Do you have anything to declare?'
words.example: We went through customs quickly.

words.clue: The place where you wait before getting on the plane
words.note: Gate numbers can change — always check the screens.
words.example: Our flight leaves from gate twelve.

words.clue: When a flight leaves later than planned
words.note: 'Delay' is both a noun and a verb: 'The flight was delayed.'
words.example: There is a two-hour delay because of fog.

words.clue: A large airport building where passengers arrive and depart
words.note: Big airports like Heathrow have several terminals.
words.example: Domestic flights leave from Terminal 2.

words.clue: Permission to enter a country, often stamped in your passport
words.note: Many countries now offer electronic visas (e-visas).
words.example: I applied for a tourist visa online.

title: Hotel Check-in
description: Book, check in and ask for what you need — politely.

words.clue: The front desk where guests check in
words.note: Also called 'the front desk' in American English.
words.example: Please leave your key at reception.

words.clue: A reservation for a room
words.note: 'Book' as a verb means to reserve: 'I booked a double room.'
words.example: I have a booking under the name Smith.

words.clue: The time you must leave your room, often 11 a.m.
words.note: Ask: 'Could I have a late checkout, please?'
words.example: Checkout is at eleven o'clock.

words.clue: First meal of the day, often included in the price
words.note: 'Is breakfast included?' is one of the most useful hotel questions.
words.example: Breakfast is served from seven to ten.

words.clue: A free room; signs say 'No ___' when the hotel is full
words.note: Plural: vacancies. It also means an open job position.
words.example: Do you have any vacancies for tonight?

words.clue: You dry yourself with it after a shower
words.note: Polite request: 'Could I have some extra towels, please?'
words.example: Could you bring me a clean towel?

words.clue: Money you pay in advance, returned if nothing is damaged
words.note: Hotels often 'hold a deposit' on your credit card.
words.example: There is a fifty-dollar deposit.

words.clue: Hotel staff member who books tours and gives local advice
words.note: The word comes from French and is pronounced kon-see-AIRZH.
words.example: The concierge recommended a great restaurant.

title: Famous Landmarks
description: Match the world's best-known sights to their cities.

words.clue: City of the Eiffel Tower
words.note: The tower was built for the 1889 World's Fair and was meant to be temporary.
words.example: We watched the tower sparkle at night in Paris.

words.clue: Indian city of the Taj Mahal
words.note: The Taj Mahal was built by Shah Jahan in memory of his wife Mumtaz Mahal.
words.example: Agra is about three hours from Delhi by train.

words.clue: Jordanian city carved into rose-red rock
words.note: Petra was the capital of the Nabataeans over 2,000 years ago.
words.example: The Treasury is the most famous building in Petra.

words.clue: Home of the Colosseum
words.note: The Colosseum could hold around 50,000 spectators.
words.example: All roads lead to Rome.

words.clue: Egyptian plateau with the Great Pyramid
words.note: The Great Pyramid was the tallest man-made structure for almost 4,000 years.
words.example: The pyramids of Giza are near Cairo.

words.clue: Australian city with a famous sail-shaped opera house
words.note: The Sydney Opera House opened in 1973.
words.example: We took a ferry across Sydney Harbour.

words.clue: Uzbek city of the Registan square
words.note: Samarkand was a key stop on the Silk Road for centuries.
words.example: The tiles in Samarkand are an incredible blue.

words.clue: Capital city of the Forbidden City
words.note: The Forbidden City has around 980 buildings.
words.example: Beijing hosted the Olympics in 2008 and 2022.

title: Ancient Civilisations
description: Pharaohs, emperors and the trade routes between them.

words.clue: Title of the kings of ancient Egypt
words.note: Note the spelling: P-H-A-R-A-O-H. The 'aoh' trips many learners.
words.example: Tutankhamun became pharaoh as a boy.

words.clue: Huge stone tomb with a square base and pointed top
words.note: Adjective: pyramidal. A 'pyramid scheme' is a type of fraud.
words.example: Thousands of workers built each pyramid.

words.clue: Greek city-state famous for its warriors
words.note: Today 'spartan' means simple and without comfort.
words.example: Boys in Sparta trained to be soldiers.

words.clue: Roman leader murdered on the Ides of March, 44 BC
words.note: His name became a title: 'Kaiser' and 'Tsar' both come from it.
words.example: Caesar crossed the Rubicon in 49 BC.

words.clue: Egyptian plant used as an early form of paper
words.note: The English word 'paper' comes from papyrus.
words.example: The scroll was written on papyrus.

words.clue: A group of countries ruled by one emperor or state
words.note: Related words: emperor, empress, imperial.
words.example: The Roman Empire lasted for centuries.

words.clue: The ___ Road linked China with the Mediterranean
words.note: The route carried paper, spices, ideas and religions, not just silk.
words.example: Merchants travelled the Silk Road by camel.

words.clue: Central American civilisation famous for its calendar
words.note: The Maya built cities like Tikal and Chichén Itzá.
words.example: The Maya studied the stars carefully.

title: Past Simple Time Travel
description: Put the verb in brackets into the past simple — history style.

words.clue: Columbus ___ (sail) across the Atlantic in 1492.
words.note: Regular verb: add -ed.
words.example: Columbus sailed with three ships.

words.clue: Gutenberg ___ (build) a printing press around 1440.
words.note: Irregular: build – built – built.
words.example: They built the bridge in two years.

words.clue: Napoleon ___ (lose) the Battle of Waterloo in 1815.
words.note: Irregular: lose – lost – lost.
words.example: Napoleon lost his last battle in Belgium.

words.clue: The ancient Romans ___ (speak) Latin.
words.note: Irregular: speak – spoke – spoken.
words.example: My grandfather spoke four languages.

words.clue: Amundsen ___ (reach) the South Pole first, in 1911.
words.note: Regular verb: reach – reached.
words.example: We reached the top at sunrise.

words.clue: The Titanic ___ (sink) in 1912.
words.note: Irregular: sink – sank – sunk.
words.example: The ship sank in less than three hours.

words.clue: Neil Armstrong ___ (walk) on the Moon in 1969.
words.note: Regular verb. Pronounced with a /t/ sound: walk-t.
words.example: He walked on the Moon for about two hours.

words.clue: Amir Timur ___ (make) Samarkand his capital.
words.note: Irregular: make – made – made.
words.example: Timur made the city a centre of art.

title: The 20th Century
description: Wars, walls, space races and the leaders who changed history.

words.clue: 'Unsinkable' ship that sank on its first voyage
words.note: About 1,500 people died when it hit an iceberg in April 1912.
words.example: The Titanic left Southampton for New York.

words.clue: NASA programme that put humans on the Moon
words.note: Apollo 11 landed on 20 July 1969.
words.example: Apollo 13 had to return without landing.

words.clue: City divided by a wall from 1961 to 1989
words.note: The wall fell on 9 November 1989.
words.example: Berlin is now the capital of a united Germany.

words.clue: Leader of India's non-violent independence movement
words.note: He was called 'Mahatma', meaning 'great soul'.
words.example: Gandhi led the Salt March in 1930.

words.clue: First artificial satellite, launched by the USSR in 1957
words.note: Its launch started the Space Race.
words.example: Sputnik sent a simple beeping signal.

words.clue: South African president who spent 27 years in prison
words.note: He received the Nobel Peace Prize in 1993.
words.example: Mandela became president in 1994.

words.clue: British prime minister during most of World War II
words.note: He also won the Nobel Prize in Literature.
words.example: Churchill gave famous speeches on the radio.

words.clue: Currency introduced in 1999
words.note: Coins and notes arrived in 2002.
words.example: You can pay in euros in Spain and Italy.

title: Great Inventions
description: Objects and discoveries that changed how we live.

words.clue: Device patented by Alexander Graham Bell in 1876
words.note: From Greek: tele (far) + phone (sound).
words.example: The first telephone call was 'Mr. Watson, come here'.

words.clue: Round invention from about 3500 BC, first used for pottery
words.note: Early wheels were solid wood; spokes came later.
words.example: The wheel made transport much easier.

words.clue: Navigation tool with a magnetic needle, invented in China
words.note: The needle points to magnetic north, not true north.
words.example: Sailors used a compass to find their way.

words.clue: First antibiotic, discovered by Alexander Fleming
words.note: Fleming found it by accident in 1928 on a mouldy dish.
words.example: Penicillin has saved millions of lives.

words.clue: Instrument Galileo used to see Jupiter's moons
words.note: From Greek: tele (far) + skopein (to look).
words.example: Through the telescope we saw Saturn's rings.

words.clue: Medicine that trains the body to fight a disease
words.note: Edward Jenner made the first one, against smallpox, in 1796.
words.example: The vaccine is given in two doses.

words.clue: Machine that turns fuel into movement
words.note: James Watt's steam engine powered the Industrial Revolution.
words.example: The car engine wouldn't start.

words.clue: Printing ___: Gutenberg's machine for books
words.note: 'The press' also means newspapers and journalists.
words.example: The printing press spread knowledge across Europe.

title: Passive Voice Workshop
description: Write the past participle: who made what, and when.

words.clue: The telephone was ___ (invent) by Bell.
words.note: Passive = be + past participle. Regular: invent – invented.
words.example: The light bulb was invented in the 19th century.

words.clue: Penicillin was ___ (discover) by Fleming in 1928.
words.note: We 'discover' what already exists and 'invent' something new.
words.example: America was discovered by Europeans in 1492.

words.clue: Paper was first ___ (make) in China.
words.note: Irregular: make – made – made.
words.example: This watch was made in Switzerland.

words.clue: The first petrol car was ___ (build) by Karl Benz.
words.note: Irregular: build – built – built.
words.example: The bridge was built in 1932.

words.clue: 'Harry Potter' was ___ (write) by J.K. Rowling.
words.note: Irregular: write – wrote – written. Note the double T.
words.example: The letter was written in pencil.

words.clue: The Eiffel Tower was ___ (design) by Gustave Eiffel's company.
words.note: The G is silent: de-ZINED.
words.example: The app was designed for children.

words.clue: Compasses were ___ (use) by sailors to navigate.
words.note: Don't confuse with 'used to' (past habit).
words.example: Steam engines were used in factories.

words.clue: Many cars will soon be ___ (drive) by computers.
words.note: Irregular: drive – drove – driven.
words.example: The bus was driven by a robot.

title: Who Invented It?
description: Name the inventors and scientists behind famous breakthroughs.

words.clue: American who developed a practical light bulb
words.note: He held over 1,000 patents.
words.example: Edison opened a research lab in Menlo Park.

words.clue: Serbian-American pioneer of alternating current (AC)
words.note: The unit of magnetic flux density is named after him.
words.example: Tesla dreamed of wireless electricity.

words.clue: Marie ___: first person to win two Nobel Prizes
words.note: She won in physics (1903) and chemistry (1911).
words.example: Curie discovered polonium and radium.

words.clue: Surname of the brothers who made the first powered flight
words.note: Orville and Wilbur flew at Kitty Hawk in 1903.
words.example: The Wright brothers' first flight lasted 12 seconds.

words.clue: Swedish inventor of dynamite who created famous prizes
words.note: He left his fortune to fund the prizes.
words.example: The Nobel Prizes are awarded each December.

words.clue: Scottish scientist who discovered penicillin
words.note: He said: 'One sometimes finds what one is not looking for.'
words.example: Fleming noticed mould killing bacteria.

words.clue: German who introduced movable-type printing in Europe
words.note: His Bible (around 1455) is one of the most valuable books.
words.example: Gutenberg changed how books were made.

words.clue: Alexander Graham ___: telephone pioneer
words.note: He was also a teacher of deaf students.
words.example: Bell was born in Edinburgh.

title: Digital World
description: The everyday words of computers and the internet.

words.clue: You type on it
words.note: QWERTY is named after the first six letters on the top row.
words.example: My keyboard is missing the letter Q.

words.clue: You click and scroll with it
words.note: Plural: mice (or 'mouses' for computer mice, informally).
words.example: Move the mouse to the top corner.

words.clue: The part of a phone or laptop that shows pictures
words.note: Phrasal verb: 'screen out' means to filter.
words.example: My screen is cracked.

words.clue: Program you use to visit websites
words.note: Chrome, Safari and Firefox are browsers.
words.example: Open the link in your browser.

words.clue: Secret word that protects your account
words.note: Strong passwords are long and unique.
words.example: Never share your password.

words.clue: To copy a file from the internet to your device
words.note: Opposite: upload.
words.example: The update takes ten minutes to download.

words.clue: Gives your phone power; it needs charging
words.note: 'My battery is dead' = it is empty.
words.example: My battery is at five percent!

words.clue: Wireless internet connection
words.note: Ask: 'What's the Wi-Fi password?'
words.example: Is there free Wi-Fi here?

title: AI & Future Tech
description: Robots, algorithms and the cloud — the vocabulary of tomorrow.

words.clue: Machine that can do tasks automatically
words.note: From the Czech word 'robota', meaning forced work.
words.example: A robot vacuums our floor.

words.clue: Step-by-step set of rules a computer follows
words.note: Named after the Persian mathematician al-Khwarizmi, born in Khorezm (today's Uzbekistan).
words.example: The algorithm recommends videos you might like.

words.clue: Facts and numbers collected for analysis
words.note: Technically plural (singular 'datum'), but often used as uncountable.
words.example: The data shows a clear trend.

words.clue: Remote servers where you store files online
words.note: 'In the cloud' means on the internet, not on your device.
words.example: My photos are backed up to the cloud.

words.clue: Flying device controlled remotely
words.note: It also means a low, continuous humming sound.
words.example: The drone filmed the wedding from above.

words.clue: Program you can have a text conversation with
words.note: A blend of 'chat' and 'robot'.
words.example: The chatbot answered my question instantly.

words.clue: Smallest dot of colour on a screen
words.note: A blend of 'picture' and 'element'.
words.example: This camera has 48 million pixels.

words.clue: Object that orbits Earth and sends signals
words.note: GPS uses about 30 satellites.
words.example: The satellite sends TV signals to Asia.

title: Comparatives in Tech
description: Faster, smaller, better — practise comparatives and superlatives.

words.clue: Phones today are ___ (small) than computers in 1990.
words.note: Short adjective: add -er.
words.example: My new laptop is smaller and lighter.

words.clue: Fibre internet is ___ (fast) than dial-up.
words.note: Short adjective: fast – faster – the fastest.
words.example: This train is faster than the plane.

words.clue: This is the ___ (big) screen in the shop.
words.note: One vowel + one consonant: double it — big, biggest.
words.example: That's the biggest TV I've ever seen.

words.clue: Tablets got ___ (cheap) every year.
words.note: Short adjective: cheap – cheaper – the cheapest.
words.example: Streaming is cheaper than cable.

words.clue: The new camera is much ___ (good) than the old one.
words.note: Irregular: good – better – the best.
words.example: This version is better than the last.

words.clue: That was the ___ (bad) update ever!
words.note: Irregular: bad – worse – the worst.
words.example: It was the worst day of my life.

words.clue: Voice typing is ___ (easy) than typing on a tiny screen.
words.note: Consonant + y → -ier.
words.example: Learning online is easier than I thought.

words.clue: This is the ___ (smart) watch on the market.
words.note: Short adjective: smart – smarter – the smartest.
words.example: She is the smartest student in class.

title: Irregular Verbs I
description: Past simple forms every learner must know.

words.clue: Past of GO
words.note: go – went – gone
words.example: We went to the beach yesterday.

words.clue: Past of BUY
words.note: buy – bought – bought. Rhymes with 'caught'.
words.example: I bought a new jacket.

words.clue: Past of THINK
words.note: think – thought – thought
words.example: I thought you were at home.

words.clue: Past of TEACH
words.note: teach – taught – taught
words.example: My mother taught me to swim.

words.clue: Past of WRITE
words.note: write – wrote – written
words.example: She wrote a letter to her friend.

words.clue: Past of BEGIN
words.note: begin – began – begun
words.example: The film began at eight.

words.clue: Past of FLY
words.note: fly – flew – flown
words.example: We flew to Istanbul.

words.clue: Past of CATCH
words.note: catch – caught – caught
words.example: He caught the last bus.

title: Phrasal Verbs
description: Find the verb that completes each phrasal verb.

words.clue: ___ up: to stop trying
words.note: 'Don't give up!' — a common phrase of encouragement.
words.example: I gave up sugar for a month.

words.clue: ___ down: to refuse an offer
words.note: 'Turn down' also means to lower the volume: 'Turn down the music!'
words.example: She turned down the job offer.

words.clue: ___ off: what a plane does when it leaves the ground
words.note: Also means to remove clothes: 'take off your shoes'.
words.example: The plane will take off in ten minutes.

words.clue: ___ out of: to have nothing left
words.note: 'We've run out of milk' — very common at home.
words.example: My phone ran out of battery.

words.clue: ___ off: to postpone
words.note: 'Don't put off until tomorrow what you can do today.'
words.example: They put off the meeting until Friday.

words.clue: ___ down: to stop working (a car or machine)
words.note: Also used for emotions: 'She broke down in tears.'
words.example: Our car broke down on the motorway.

words.clue: ___ out: to understand or solve
words.note: Informal, very common in American English.
words.example: I can't figure out this puzzle.

words.clue: ___ on: to continue
words.note: 'Carry on' is also a polite 'please continue'.
words.example: Carry on reading, please.

title: Tricky Plurals
description: Irregular and spelling-change plurals.

words.clue: Plural of CHILD
words.note: Old English plural ending -ren.
words.example: The children are playing outside.

words.clue: Plural of MOUSE
words.note: Same pattern: louse – lice.
words.example: There are mice in the kitchen!

words.clue: Plural of TOOTH
words.note: Vowel change: oo → ee, like foot – feet.
words.example: Brush your teeth twice a day.

words.clue: Plural of WOMAN
words.note: Pronounced WIM-in.
words.example: Three women started the company.

words.clue: Usual plural of PERSON
words.note: 'Persons' exists but is very formal.
words.example: Many people visit the museum.

words.clue: Plural of KNIFE
words.note: -fe / -f often becomes -ves: wife – wives, leaf – leaves.
words.example: Put the knives in the drawer.

words.clue: Plural of CITY
words.note: Consonant + y → -ies.
words.example: Tokyo and Delhi are huge cities.

words.clue: Plural of POTATO
words.note: Add -es: tomato – tomatoes, hero – heroes.
words.example: I peeled the potatoes.

title: Small Talk Starters
description: Polite words that open every conversation. Say each one aloud.

words.clue: The most common greeting
words.note: Informal options: hi, hey. Formal: good morning.
words.example: Hello, nice to meet you!

words.clue: Magic word that makes a request polite
words.note: Put it at the start or end: 'Please sit down' / 'Water, please.'
words.example: Could you help me, please?

words.clue: Informal way to say 'thank you'
words.note: Reply with 'You're welcome' or 'No problem'.
words.example: Thanks a lot for your help!

words.clue: Word to apologise or to ask someone to repeat
words.note: 'Sorry?' with rising intonation means 'Can you repeat that?'
words.example: Sorry, I'm late.

words.clue: You're ___: reply to 'thank you'
words.note: Also used to greet guests: 'Welcome to our home!'
words.example: You're welcome, any time.

words.clue: What you say when you leave
words.note: Casual: bye, see you, take care.
words.example: Goodbye and have a nice day!

words.clue: ___ me: to get attention politely
words.note: Use it before a question to a stranger.
words.example: Excuse me, where is the station?

words.clue: British people's favourite small-talk topic
words.note: 'Lovely weather, isn't it?' — a classic opener.
words.example: What's the weather like today?

title: At the Restaurant
description: Order food, ask for the bill and leave a tip.

words.clue: List of dishes you can order
words.note: Ask: 'Could we see the menu, please?'
words.example: The menu has three vegetarian dishes.

words.clue: Person who brings your food
words.note: Gender-neutral: server.
words.example: The waiter recommended the fish.

words.clue: Ask for the ___ when you want to pay (British English)
words.note: Americans say 'the check'.
words.example: Could we have the bill, please?

words.clue: To ask for food in a restaurant
words.note: 'Are you ready to order?' 'Yes, I'll have the soup.'
words.example: I'd like to order a salad.

words.clue: Sweet course at the end of a meal
words.note: Don't confuse with 'desert' (sand). Dessert has two S's — 'sweet stuff'.
words.example: What would you like for dessert?

words.clue: Small dish before the main course (UK)
words.note: Americans say 'appetizer'.
words.example: We shared a starter.

words.clue: Extra money for good service
words.note: In the US it's usually 15–20%.
words.example: We left a ten percent tip.

words.clue: Someone who doesn't eat meat
words.note: A vegan eats no animal products at all.
words.example: Do you have any vegetarian options?

title: Everyday Idioms
description: Complete the idiom, then use it in a sentence out loud.

words.clue: Break the ___: start a conversation with strangers
words.note: Icebreaker games help groups relax.
words.example: He told a joke to break the ice.

words.clue: A piece of ___: very easy
words.note: Similar: 'easy as pie'.
words.example: The test was a piece of cake.

words.clue: Under the ___: feeling slightly ill
words.note: Originally a sailors' expression.
words.example: I'm feeling a bit under the weather.

words.clue: Once in a blue ___: very rarely
words.note: A 'blue moon' is a second full moon in one month.
words.example: I only eat fast food once in a blue moon.

words.clue: Spill the ___: reveal a secret
words.note: Very informal, popular in social media slang.
words.example: Come on, spill the beans!

words.clue: Cost an arm and a ___: very expensive
words.note: Never literal!
words.example: That phone cost an arm and a leg.

words.clue: The ball is in your ___: it's your decision now
words.note: From tennis.
words.example: I've made my offer — the ball is in your court.

words.clue: Hit the ___: go to bed
words.note: 'Get the sack' means to lose your job — different idiom!
words.example: I'm tired, I'm going to hit the sack.

title: World Capitals
description: One capital city from every corner of the globe.

words.clue: Capital of Uzbekistan
words.note: Its name means 'stone city'.
words.example: Tashkent has a beautiful metro system.

words.clue: Capital of Japan
words.note: The Greater Tokyo Area is the world's largest metropolitan area.
words.example: Tokyo hosted the 2020 Olympics in 2021.

words.clue: Capital of Egypt, on the river Nile
words.note: Its Arabic name, al-Qāhira, means 'the victorious'.
words.example: Cairo is the largest city in Africa.

words.clue: Capital of Canada (not Toronto!)
words.note: Queen Victoria chose it in 1857.
words.example: Parliament Hill is in Ottawa.

words.clue: Capital of Australia (not Sydney!)
words.note: It was built as a compromise between Sydney and Melbourne.
words.example: Canberra is a planned city.

words.clue: Capital of the United Kingdom
words.note: The Romans called it Londinium.
words.example: London has over 170 museums.

words.clue: Capital of Spain
words.note: It sits almost exactly in the centre of the country.
words.example: The Prado museum is in Madrid.

words.clue: Capital of Brazil since 1960
words.note: Designed in the shape of an aeroplane (or a bird).
words.example: Brasilia was built in just 41 months.

title: Wonders of Nature
description: Mountains, rivers, deserts and seas.

words.clue: World's highest mountain
words.note: 8,849 metres high, on the border of Nepal and China.
words.example: Climbing Everest takes about two months.

words.clue: Rainforest and river in South America
words.note: The Amazon carries more water than any other river.
words.example: The Amazon is home to millions of species.

words.clue: Largest hot desert in the world
words.note: 'Sahara' means 'desert' in Arabic, so 'Sahara Desert' is a bit repetitive!
words.example: The Sahara is almost as big as the USA.

words.clue: Long river flowing north through Egypt
words.note: Usually called the longest river in the world (about 6,650 km).
words.example: Ancient Egypt depended on the Nile.

words.clue: Largest and deepest ocean
words.note: Magellan named it 'peaceful' (pacific).
words.example: The Pacific covers a third of Earth's surface.

words.clue: Mountain that can erupt with lava
words.note: Plural: volcanoes. From Vulcan, the Roman god of fire.
words.example: The volcano erupted last year.

words.clue: Slowly moving river of ice
words.note: Pronounced GLAY-see-er (UK) or GLAY-sher (US).
words.example: The glacier is melting quickly.

words.clue: Central Asian sea that has shrunk dramatically
words.note: Once the fourth-largest lake on Earth, it lost most of its water after the 1960s.
words.example: Ships now lie in the sand of the old Aral Sea.
